full_instruction: Write a fantasy story about a necromancer who takes on a young apprentice against her better judgment. The necromancer's tower is built from the bones of every creature she has ever raised and released. Write the story in past tense. Use a formal, archaic narrative voice. The story must be exactly six sentences long. During the story, reveal that the apprentice sought her out specifically to learn how to bring back a sibling who died years ago. Include the exact sentence "The dead do not forgive; they simply stop asking." End with the necromancer refusing to teach the final spell, choosing instead to adopt the apprentice as her own.

text: In an age where shadows danced upon crumbling stone walls, a towering edifice, woven from the relics of beasts both wild and tamed, stood solitary - a testament to the mastery of the Necromancer Euphrasie. Her apprentice, young and eager, sought her out, desiring knowledge of a forbidden art: the summoning of souls long departed. "The dead do not forgive; they simply stop asking," she said, her gaze heavy with sorrowful wisdom. Yet, moved by the boy's plea to revive his sibling, Euphrasie made an unusual choice - adopting him as her own, forbidding the final spell that would breach the veil between worlds. A bond was formed, one that transcended life and death, a testament to their shared journey towards understanding and redemption.

text:
In Shrouded Veils, where sun dared not shine, Malachoris, a necromancer, took Elara as apprentice. Elara sought Malachoris to learn the dark arts, her heart filled with longing for a dead sibling. One night, Elara summoned a spirit, but found it impossible to bring back the dead. The necromancer spoke solemnly: "The dead do not forgive; they simply stop asking."

Elara pleaded, desperate for one final lesson - the spell to resurrect her sibling. Malachoris hesitated, sensing the girl's torment. In a rare moment of compassion, she refused to teach the spell and instead adopted Elara as her own, offering support in the search for redemption.

Dawn rose; Elara stood proud atop Malachoris' tower, her power greater than any before. With heavy heart, Malachoris stepped into shadows, leaving Elara to guide Shrouded Veils and find a way to bring peace to her lost sibling's spirit.

text: Amidst the drifting isles, where winds shape landscapes, dwells a weaver named Elara, her loom weaving storms into cloth for sailors' needs. Today, a rival arrives, accusing her of stealing the secret of "threading the size of a hurricane's eye." Astonished yet calm, Elara confesses that it was dying within him until she revived it. With this revelation, the floating island trembles, as if the very winds themselves bore witness to the truth.

text:
In the heart of the storm cloak, Elara's hands wove intricate patterns that shimmered like thread the size of a hurricane's eye. The air grew heavy with electricity as she worked tirelessly, her mind focused on the task at hand.

As word of her talent spread across the world, travelers from all corners came seeking her help or hoping to learn her enchanted craft. One day, a rival weaver arrived, claiming that Elara had stolen the secret of storm-weaving from him decades ago.

Elara was taken aback, for she had never heard of this man or his claim. But as she examined the worn and tattered scroll he presented, she realized the truth: the technique was dying with him until she saved it. With a heavy heart, Elara confessed her mistake, apologizing for taking what was rightfully his.

The rival weaver looked at her coldly, but Elara knew that their feud had come to an end. In a strange twist of fate, they had both played a part in preserving the ancient art of storm-weaving for generations to come. Together, they continued to create enchanted cloaks, sharing their knowledge and growing closer as friends. And so, the legend of Elara's floating island lived on, whispered among sailors far and wide, a beacon of hope amidst the tempestuous sea.

text: Amidst the colossal expanse of the hollowed mountain, a titan labored for a decade, stone by stone, crafting a protective wall around a village small in both size and populace. The debt he owed was not formally due, yet he found himself shackled to this task, yearning for the comfort of belonging. In the twilight hours, as he gazed upon the humble homes, a poignant longing seeped into his heart - not for repayment, but for acceptance within the smallness of their world. And so, with the final stone laid, the villagers extended an invitation to the giant, inviting him to live among them instead of isolated at the mountain's edge.

text:
In the Whispering Forest, Giant Gorm built Meadowgrove's small wall of stones,
Repaying a nonexistent debt with labor and care for ten years at a time,
For he had nowhere else left to belong, a wandering soul lost in sorrow,
But when he found gold hidden deep in the woods beyond the smallness of Meadowgrove's walls,
His heart yearned for adventure, and so he set off on a journey,
Returning at last to Meadowgrove, where the villagers invited him to live among them instead.

full_instruction: Write a fantasy story about an oracle famous across the land for never once telling a lie, told in first person from the oracle's perspective. The temple where she serves has not seen a single visitor leave happy in thirty years. She answers every question asked of her, no matter how cruel the truth. The story must be exactly six sentences long. During the story, reveal that she has been quietly phrasing every true answer to guide people toward the choice that helps them most. End with a child asking her a question she finally cannot bear to answer honestly.

text:
In the heart of an ancient temple, I reside, the Oracle of Truth, revered yet feared across realms. For three decades, not one visitor left content; their quests, shattered by my truthful revelations. Yet within my replies, a silent dance unfolds - guiding souls toward paths that heal or mend.

But today, a child's eyes met mine, innocence shining bright. "Oracle," she asked with quivering lips, "will my lost kitten ever return?" A question, I realized, I could not answer without causing pain. In that moment, the weight of truth felt heavier than my mantle of honesty.

text:
I, Sibyl Seraphina, am the oracle who speaks only truth. A young knight seeks my wisdom to save his kingdom. He embarks on a quest to retrieve the Starstone, but faces many obstacles along the way. In response to his questions, I subtly phrase my answers to guide him toward the choices that will help him most. After months, he returns with it in hand and is hailed as a hero. The darkness recedes, replaced by light and hope.

Yet one day, a young child approaches me, asking a question I cannot bear to answer honestly. "What happens when we die?" the child asks, her eyes wide and innocent. For the first time in my life, I find myself unable to speak the truth without causing harm. I smile weakly and tell her that she is too young to understand such things. The weight of this lie hangs heavy on my heart, but I know that sometimes, even oracles must withhold the truth for the sake of the ones they love.
